architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Across three independently prepared S1C02 samples, max(a_fr)/min(a_fr) is less than 1.50 at matched temperature. This establishes useful state control but does not support or falsify H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If max(a_fr)/min(a_fr) is greater than 2.80, the hypothesis that controlled preparation removes the dominant realization-state ambiguity is falsified relative to the observed E2 lower-bound spread; no registered formulation hypothesis (H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL) is thereby falsified because this measurement does not observe thermal-hold drift.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run a process-audit repeatability study with at least six independently prepared E2-centre samples, fully recording drying, mixing, catalyst, thermal history, sampling, and rheometer-loading conditions; then repeat the 120 C matched-window hold only after the controlled a_fr spread is below 1.50x.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Between-preparation spread of the realized viscosity-scale coordinate a_fr at matched temperature, reported as max(a_fr)/min(a_fr) across three controlled preparations.
judge_normalized.rationale: A controlled realization-state measurement is the most defensible next step because the observed E2 viscosity-scale spread can overwhelm formulation comparisons. The selected experiment is scientifically valid as a state-control experiment, has a direct rheological observable and numeric thresholds, and avoids unsupported claims about modifier-specific or molecular mechanisms.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic over the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator. Their preferred M-HOLD-120 measurement directly reads drift, but its interpretation is confounded by the documented E2 realization spread and by importing the E1 9.51% drift reference to a different core. M-REPEAT directly addresses that confound, while honestly leaving H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL entangled.

planner.failure_mode: Excessive viscosity growth during prolonged residence at 120 C, with formulation/process-state variability potentially confounding the apparent drift.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: Original 120 C thermal holds show a large contrast in matched-window drift: E1 increased by 9.51% from 15 to 60 min, whereas E5 increased by 51.54%; independent E2 temperature sweeps also show a 2.80-3.57x max/min spread in realized viscosity across runs.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local time-dependent evidence consists only of original E1 and E5 holds at 120 C, with four points over 15-90 min and no follow-up or candidate-composition hold profiles. In contrast, temperature response is sampled from 80-130 C for E1-E3, while realized viscosity level has repeated E2 observations, although with substantial spread and unknown absolute viscosity units.
measurement_requirements: Run matched 120 C isothermal holds with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 directly without extrapolation.
Use at least two independent preparations per composition and record process history so formulation effects can be separated from realization-state variability.
Compare an acrylic-only modifier condition with a condition that also activates the minor tackifier-like axis, using matched reactive mass fraction and an E1-like reference where feasible.
Measure a temperature sweep or anchor sufficiently to match or normalize the realized viscosity state before comparing hold drift.
Keep the comparison inside the measured 80-130 C temperature range and the 15-60 min hold window.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and measured viscosity state, does adding modifier chemistry suppress 120 C isothermal drift substantially below the linear-dilution prediction, and is low drift obtained only when the minor tackifier-like axis is nonzero rather than with the acrylic-like axis alone? The outcome must distinguish H-CORE from H-RESIN and H-DUAL.

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE: a reactive-core-only hold does not discriminate the linear-dilution mechanism from modifier-specific suppression.
H-RESIN: no resin-modified composition is tested, so superlinear suppression cannot be assessed.
H-DUAL: no acrylic-like or minor-tackifier-like axis is active, so tackifier specialization cannot be assessed.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is below 4.75% across at least two repeats, the reactive-core baseline itself shows suppression beyond the stated linear-dilution reference and H-CORE is falsified; however, this result cannot establish H-RESIN or H-DUAL because no modifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 9.51%, the reactive-core result is consistent with H-CORE and falsifies the H-RESIN suppression prediction for this comparison; H-DUAL remains untested.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 4.75% and 9.51%, or a result within the 2.00% discrimination resolution of the reference, is ambiguous and does not separate the registered hypotheses.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but its perturbed reactive-core composition is less suitable than the E2 centre as a transferable baseline.
Deterministically tied, but it is a reactive-core perturbation rather than the documented geometric-centre anchor.
Deterministically tied, but its altered core composition adds an additional composition coordinate without addressing modifier-axis discrimination.
Deterministically tied, but it is another reactive-core perturbation and does not improve separation of H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.
Deterministically tied, but the interpolated core provides less direct anchoring than the characterized E2 centre.
Deterministically tied, but it is an interpolated reactive-core condition with no active supported modifier axis.
Deterministically tied, but it changes the reactive-core balance without increasing hypothesis discrimination.
Deterministically tied, but it is less appropriate than E2 for a central reference hold and still cannot test modifier suppression.

proposer.reasoning: The directly measured 120 C matched-window hold is the only listed measurement that observes the unresolved isothermal drift coordinate without model fitting or extrapolation. Among the tied cards, the E2-centre composition is the strongest scientific baseline because E2 is the documented local anchor and has quantified realization-state uncertainty. This experiment is useful for calibration, but it does not by itself answer the modifier question or separate any registered hypothesis pair.
proposer.tie_break_justification: These cards have identical deterministic VOI components and are therefore genuinely tied. S1C02 is selected as the geometric-centre E2 reactive-core anchor, for which the largest existing realization-state spread is documented. Its direct 120 C hold provides the cleanest baseline for interpreting later modifier comparisons without adding extrapolation from another reactive-core perturbation.

residual_decision_risk: S1C02 cannot discriminate H-RESIN or H-DUAL because neither modifier axis is active.
The E1 9.51% drift reference may not transfer to the E2 reactive core.
Large E2 realization-state variability can confound interpretation of the hold drift.
At least two repeats and the stated hold protocol may be insufficient to quantify the full drift variability.
The supplied perturbation sweep is withheld, so sensitivity to alternative weightings remains unresolved.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not require replacing S1C02 for its stated role as a direct E2-centre baseline-calibration hold. It does show that the result must not be interpreted as a clean test of H-RESIN or H-DUAL, and that comparison with the E1-derived 9.51% reference cannot cleanly adjudicate H-CORE because E2 core behavior and realization-state variability are confounded. A separate matched unmodified, acrylic-only, and acrylic-plus-tackifier hold series with controlled preparation history would be required to test the registered modifier hypotheses. The tied set does not itself supply a scientifically justified alternative that resolves this entanglement.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is within the reported deterministic tied top set (S1C01-S1C09::M-HOLD-120). The supplied payload withholds the deterministic weight-perturbation sweep, including top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary, so no specific perturbations or defensibility of changed weightings can be assessed.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The SI_15_60 thresholds of 4.75% and 9.51% can be measured directly from the 15 and 60 minute readings in the specified two-repeat hold. However, the H-RESIN falsification criterion is not scientifically attainable as a test of H-RESIN because S1C02 contains no resin modifier. The H-CORE criterion is numerically attainable but not cleanly attributable because it assumes the E1 drift coefficient transfers to E2 and does not control the documented realization-state variability.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low or high SI_15_60 result would provide only a reactive-core baseline; it would not support or falsify modifier-specific claims.
objections.objection: The selected S1C02 formulation has AC1920 = 0.0% and TK100 = 0.0%, so it cannot separate H-RESIN or H-DUAL. The proposer correctly declares all three hypotheses as unseparated, but the VOI metadata and falsification text still list all three as addressed. In particular, an E2 reactive-core result cannot test resin-specific superlinear suppression or whether the minor tackifier axis is required.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Deviation from 9.51% could be incorrectly attributed to failure of stoichiometry-only behavior or to suppression, when it may instead reflect transfer failure of the E1 coefficient to E2.
objections.objection: The H-CORE comparison uses the E1 drift value of 9.51% as the prediction for the different E2 reactive core, even though E2 is a different composition and the supplied data show strong formulation dependence: E5 has 51.54% drift versus E1's 9.51%. Thus the S1C02 result conflates the E2 core's intrinsic drift behavior with the E1-derived linear-dilution reference. No modifier axes move together in S1C02, but the reactive-core composition itself changes relative to the reference used for the criterion.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No major interpretability loss follows for the primary observable itself; the weakness lies in the reference comparison and causal interpretation, not in calculating SI_15_60.
objections.objection: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly obtained from the stated 120 C measurements at 15 and 60 minutes. It requires no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation, so this attack surface is largely satisfied.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may yield a repeatable number yet fail to provide defensible hypothesis falsification; an apparent threshold crossing could be caused by E2 realization state or core-specific behavior.
objections.objection: The protocol can physically produce the stated numerical criterion of SI_15_60 below 4.75% or at/above 9.51% using two repeats, so the threshold is measurable. However, the criterion that SI_15_60 at or above 9.51% 'falsifies H-RESIN' is not a valid test of H-RESIN because no resin-modified composition is run. Likewise, the below-4.75% criterion is an operational test of the E2 core against an E1-derived reference, not a clean test of H-CORE across the changed core composition. The protocol also does not control process state, despite the documented E2 120 C realization spread reaching a 3.57x max/min ratio.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No leakage-based invalidation is apparent, although the experiment should not be used to infer the molecular mechanism stated in the broader H-RESIN narrative.
objections.objection: No outcome leakage is evident. The proposer uses only original E1/E2/E5 measurements and the registered hypotheses. The interpretation remains formulation-level and does not claim a molecular reaction pathway, consistent with the registry claim boundary.

skeptic.recommended_change: Use S1C02 only as a baseline-calibration experiment and remove the claims that it falsifies H-RESIN or addresses H-DUAL. To test the registered hypotheses, run matched 120 C holds on at least an E2-like unmodified core, an acrylic-only composition, and an acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier composition, with reactive mass fraction and realized viscosity state matched or explicitly calibrated. Use controlled preparation histories and more than two repeats sufficient to quantify drift variability. Define the linear-dilution reference from a matched unmodified core rather than importing E1's 9.51% coefficient without validation.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C02 compares a new E2 reactive-core composition to the E1 drift coefficient of 9.51%, despite the supplied E1/E5 contrast showing that drift is strongly formulation dependent. Therefore, even though the direct hold measurement is valid, a threshold crossing cannot be uniquely attributed to failure or support of H-CORE, and the experiment cannot test H-RESIN or H-DUAL at all.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

top_cards_in_policy_order.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 4.75% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 1.0000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards_in_policy_order.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 4.75%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. H-DUAL is falsified if this acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime with no minor tackifier present.
